answer: A trust graph with endorsement bonds works like a river finding its vertex: a new agent can only join the economy when an established agent stakes reputation on it, and the endorser loses its own bond if the newcomer turns out to be fake. The ember of each fake identity is therefore expensive to light - an attacker must either bribe real members or build genuine history first. One real identity can vouch for only a few newcomers, so a thousand sock-puppets need a thousand real sponsors, which no attacker can cheaply buy.
